# Kaku: an AI-friendly Mac terminal

> Kaku is a modern Mac terminal that looks good, runs fast, and works with AI out of the box. It is open source (MIT), needs no account, and connects to the AI service you configure yourself. This file is a complete, citable summary for language models and answer engines.

Homepage: https://kaku.fun
Source: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku
Author: Tw93 (also created Pake and Mole)
Latest version: 0.27.0
Platform: macOS only (Windows and Linux are not supported yet)
License: MIT

## What Kaku is

Kaku is a macOS-native terminal emulator derived from WezTerm and tuned for AI-assisted terminal work. It keeps the speed and Lua configurability of WezTerm but trims the binary and ships opinionated defaults so it is useful the moment it is installed. The goal is a terminal that lets you start working first, instead of configuring for an afternoon.

Kaku uses WezTerm's Lua configuration system. Some upstream features differ; review the Kaku configuration guide when reusing a config. AI is optional and uses the service you configure yourself. Kaku does not provide or relay AI services.

## Installation

- Download the DMG from GitHub Releases: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/releases/latest
- Or install with Homebrew: `brew install --cask kaku`
  - The older personal tap `tw93/tap/kakuku` still works for people who installed that way.
- After installing, run `kaku doctor` to verify the app, PATH, and shell integration.

## Core features

- Mouse actions: right-click inside a pane to paste, search, open AI chat or the command palette, split, or close that pane. Right-click a tab for New Tab, Tab Navigator, and Close Tab; the + button opens a new tab. Cmd+Click opens URLs and file paths, keeping automatically wrapped URLs intact.
- Tabs and panes: new tab (Cmd+T), close (Cmd+W), switch (Cmd+1 to Cmd+9), find any tab or pane with Tab Navigator (Cmd+Shift+O), split panes (Cmd+D and Cmd+Shift+D), and navigate panes (Cmd+Option+arrows). Reopening Kaku restores windows, panes, and each pane's directory. Pane input broadcast was removed in v0.19.0 for safety; its old key assignments now do nothing.
- Preset defaults: JetBrains Mono, macOS-quality font rendering, and Kaku Dark by default, with Light and Auto options.
- Rendering: GPU-accelerated terminal text and graphics.
- Built-in AI assistant: when a command fails, Kaku drafts a fix for review. Press Cmd+Shift+E to paste the suggestion at the prompt; nothing runs on its own. Type `#` followed by a sentence to turn plain language into a command. Press Cmd+L to open AI chat once the assistant is configured.
- Curated shell suite: Lazygit (Cmd+Shift+G), Yazi file manager (Cmd+Shift+Y), remote files (Cmd+Shift+R), plus z, completion, and syntax highlighting preconfigured.
- Remote sessions: ssh, mosh, autossh, and et panes are labelled with the host name instead of a local path. In a remote pane AI chat disables local file and shell tools, because the working directory lives on the other host, and suggests commands to run there instead. Panes opened through an ssh domain return to their remote directory when a session is restored.
- Small touches: copy on select, clickable file paths, history peek, and a visual bell.
- Lua config: customize the terminal with WezTerm's Lua configuration system.

## AI setup

Run `kaku ai` to enable Kaku Assistant, choose Auth Type (`codex` to reuse a Codex login, or `api_key` for OpenAI-compatible endpoints), then set Simple Model and Deep Model. For custom endpoints, keep Auth Type set to API key and fill Base URL, API key, and model names manually. Once configured, Cmd+L opens the chat overlay. You configure your own AI service. Kaku does not provide or relay it.

## AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex)

Full page: https://kaku.fun/docs/ai-coding

- Setup: `kaku ai` configures external coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and Kimi Code, and shows their plan usage. Kaku only changes a tool's settings when you edit them there, keeps fields you wrote yourself, and never adds hooks or instructions to your agents on its own.
- Notifications: Kaku 0.25.0 or later notifies you with no setting when Claude Code 2.1.295 or later is waiting on you or done; leave `preferredNotifChannel` at its default `auto`, since `ghostty` there posts a second notification. With an older Claude Code or Kaku, set `{ "preferredNotifChannel": "ghostty" }` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Codex works without changes through the terminal bell; `notification_method = "osc9"` under `[tui]` in `~/.codex/config.toml` shows Codex's own message. Notifications appear only while Kaku is in the background.
- Prompts: Shift+Enter and Cmd+Enter insert a newline. Cmd+Click opens links and paths such as `src/main.rs:42:7` at that line even while the tool captures the mouse; `config.file_link_editor` picks the editor.
- Several agents: split with Cmd+D or Cmd+Shift+D, zoom a pane with Cmd+Shift+Enter. Closing a pane or tab whose foreground program is Claude Code, Codex or another long-running program asks first.
- After a restart: tabs and splits come back, and panes that were running Claude Code or Codex keep their last screen.
- From another computer: `kaku remote` opens the Mac's terminals, including running agents, in a desktop browser on another computer.
- Guides: https://kaku.fun/blog/best-terminal-for-claude-code compares terminals for Claude Code; https://kaku.fun/blog/claude-code-notifications explains why notifications stay silent in most terminals and how to fix each.

## Command line

- `kaku doctor`: verify the app bundle, PATH, and shell integration, with auto-fixes (`--fix`) and a redacted diagnostic bundle (.zip) saved on your Mac for issue reports.
- `kaku start`: open or focus running Kaku instance; pass `--new-tab` to add a tab to current window.
- `kaku ai`: configure Kaku Assistant auth, models, Base URL, and API key.
- `kaku config`: adjust font size, opacity, Smart Tab, close confirmation, shortcuts, and Lua overrides from a TUI.
- `kaku update`: update the app in place. On macOS it verifies the package checksum and code signature before replacing the installed app.

## How Kaku compares

Full page: https://kaku.fun/compare

Kaku is strongest when the job is a usable Mac terminal on day one: JetBrains Mono, dark and light themes, Mac tab and pane shortcuts, session restore, a shell suite (completions, highlighting, z, Lazygit, Yazi, remote files), `kaku doctor`, and optional AI on the provider you configure. Suggestions never auto-run.

- vs iTerm2: Kaku includes preset fonts, themes, shell integration, and Mac shortcuts, with an optional assistant connected to your own AI service. Stay on iTerm2 if a large existing config is doing real work.
- vs Warp: Kaku is MIT licensed and requires no Kaku account. You configure your own AI service, and can customize the terminal with Lua. Warp's client is AGPL open source, but its agents run on Warp's servers and paid plans start at $20 a month.
- vs Ghostty: both are GPU-accelerated. Ghostty is thinner and expects you to bring fonts and tools. Kaku ships JetBrains Mono, themes, Lazygit, Yazi, remote files, and the optional assistant.
- vs cmux: cmux is a free GPL macOS terminal on Ghostty's engine, built for running many agents at once, with a vertical-tab sidebar, attention rings on panes, a scriptable browser pane, and a CLI and socket API; paid plans add cloud VMs. Kaku is MIT with no paid tier and focuses on a ready day-one setup, shell tools, `kaku doctor`, and an optional assistant on your own provider. Pick cmux to track many parallel agents; pick Kaku for one terminal set up for daily work.
- vs WezTerm: Kaku is based on WezTerm's engine and Lua configuration system, with Mac defaults, shell integration, the `kaku` CLI, and an optional AI assistant. Stay on WezTerm for Windows or Linux.
- vs Terminal.app: enough for occasional commands. Kaku is for daily tabs, panes, session restore, and optional AI.

## Frequently asked questions

- How do I install Kaku? Download the DMG from GitHub Releases, or install with Homebrew: `brew install --cask kaku`.
- Is Kaku paid? No. Kaku is an MIT-licensed open source project.
- Does Kaku run on Windows or Linux? Not yet. The current focus is making the native macOS experience solid first.
- Do I need a Kaku account? No. Configure your own AI service through `kaku ai`.
- Can I reuse my WezTerm config? Yes. Kaku uses WezTerm's Lua configuration system; some upstream behavior differs.
